title: Every USB Port Color Explained (White, Black, Blue & More)
description: USB port colors are not a design choice. Each color tells you the speed and the era of the port.
cta: Full video on YouTube: link in bio

compare.say: You have probably seen a blue USB port sitting right next to a black one, and assumed the colors were just a design choice. They are not.

grid.say: Every color has a meaning. Speed, power, sometimes both. This is every USB port color, explained. Starting with the oldest one of all.

chapters.name: White
chapters.label: WHITE
chapters.hook: White USB ports are the oldest ones still alive.

beats.say: The white one. On an old computer it looks like cheap plastic. It is not. White is the original. The very first USB ever made.
White means USB one point zero, straight from nineteen ninety six. Spot one, and you are looking at a real piece of computer history.
beats.head: USB 1.0
beats.label: 1996 — the first generation

beats.say: Before USB, every device had its own plug. One port for the printer. Another for the keyboard. A third one for the mouse.
beats.head: Before USB

beats.say: Top speed? One and a half megabytes per second. A single photo from your phone would take three whole seconds to copy.
beats.label: USB 1.0 top speed

beats.say: But here is the twist. USB one never died. Car stereos and cheap MP3 players still use it today. Why pay for a faster chip, when the slow one does the job?
beats.head: It never died

outro.say: So next time you see a white port, remember. That is not cheap plastic. That is the founder.
